title: A member who stays away for a few months can stop getting 'Time to train' reminders, and nothing tells them
what: Newer Android phones pause an app that has not been opened for about three months: its permissions are taken back and it can no longer ring alarms or show notifications from the background. The reminders are built to 'keep coming however long the app stays closed', but nothing in the app checks for this pause, asks the member to keep MettleUp exempt, or mentions it in the alert check-up. So the members the reminder is meant to win back are the ones who silently stop getting it. Read from the code only; the phone behaviour itself needs a real phone left unopened to confirm.
expected: When reminders are on, the app checks whether Android may pause it when unused and offers the member a one-tap way to keep it allowed; the alert check-up lists it like the other blockers.
who: members with reminders on who stop opening the app
how_often: after about three months without opening the app, on Android 11 and newer
fix_line: Check Android's unused-app pause when reminders are switched on and in the alert check-up, and offer the settings link to keep MettleUp allowed

title: The 'Gym right now' widget says 'Last checked' with a time but no day
what: Once the gym reading is over 30 minutes old the widget says 'Check again' and 'Last checked 6:05 pm'. It never says which day. After a weekend or months without opening the app, a reading from days ago looks like one from earlier today.
expected: An old reading says its day too when it is not from today, for example 'Last checked Mon 6:05 pm' or 'Last checked 3 days ago'.
how_often: every time the app was not opened since an earlier day
fix_line: Add the day to the 'Last checked' line when the reading is not from today

title: With the watch app updated but the phone app not, the watch's minus 15 seconds button quietly does nothing
what: The watch's minus 15 seconds button arrived on 3 November. A phone app from before then does not know that button: it only writes a note in its own log and does nothing. The phone tells the watch only when a Done fails, so the member presses minus 15 seconds and the rest does not change, with no message. The watch app and the phone app update on their own in Google Play, so different versions can meet.
expected: The watch shows only buttons the phone it talks to can carry out, or shows a short 'Update MettleUp on your phone' note when the phone does not understand a button.
who: members with a watch whose phone app is older than the watch app
how_often: every minus 15 seconds press on such a pair
fix_line: Answer every watch button the phone does not understand so the watch can show an update note

items.reason: Update: a running rest and the live card come back after an app update; old notification channels are deleted and new ones made, so older versions move over cleanly; saved phone choices from before the 'chosen' flag are read correctly. Sideload: the in-app Play update says 'no update' on a GitHub copy, but that copy cannot reach a Play watch app (existing finding). Watch and phone on different versions: newer phone fields are ignored by an older watch, but a newer watch button on an older phone is silently dropped (new finding). Panel cache after deploy does not apply to the phone's native parts.

Plan end: a lapsed Plus subscription is no longer listed by Play, and an unanswered Play reads as unknown, not as lapsed; a payment approved while the app stays closed is an existing finding. Member leaves the gym: the gym home-screen shortcut is greyed out and the widget shows 'No gym yet'. Changing phone: a restore keeps Health Connect off and sets reminders again (the new phone's permission gap is an existing finding). Year end and leap day: the widgets redraw after each local midnight and reminders repeat by weekday, so neither breaks. Not opened for 6 months: Health Connect reads page through everything since the last read; the Today widget's old targets are an existing finding; reminders can stop when Android pauses the unused app and the gym widget hides the day of its last reading (new findings). Staff leaving and the gym's trial do not touch the phone's native parts.

Each new rule in this area reaches existing installs: the new alert sounds use new channels and the old ones are deleted on the next run; renamed channels are renamed in place; a widget placed by an older version without its key asks before starting a workout and gets the key on the next refresh; older saved reminder choices are kept as the member's own.

Existing members get a path: channels move on the next app run, the gym widget from an older app says 'Open the app once', and losing exact alarms in 0.56.1 is answered by the rest timer's ask and the alert check-up.
Rule applied: no new-installs-only fix without a path was found in this area.

The only 'new for you' marks here are the watch update notice and the Play update card. A brand-new watch app writes its version on first open or when the phone asks, and the Play card shows only when Play itself offers a newer version, so a fresh install sees neither. The What's new dots live in another area.
Rule applied: no mark in this area flags something not new to the member.
